name: Song Doc
kicker: Fishing port on the Ông Đốc
summary: Walk the stilt houses on the Ông Đốc, a daytime stop, and come for the whale boats when the rite is on. The procession leaves Lăng Ông Nam Hải for the fish port and the sea. In 2026 it fell on 2 April, the 15th of the second lunar month. The next solar date moves with that lunar pair.
getThere: West of the city, on the Ông Đốc.
heroCaption: Stilt houses along the river at Sông Đốc

notice.title: The whale boats go out on the rite days
notice.body: The procession runs on the 14th and 15th of the second lunar month. On another day the visit is the river and the stilt houses.

body: The town is the west-coast fishing port on the Ông Đốc. Houses stand over the river. The whale temple is Lăng Ông Nam Hải. On an ordinary day you walk the bank. On the rite days the boats escort Ông from the temple to the fish port and then to sea.

The rite sits on the 14th and 15th of the second lunar month. In 2026 the 15th was 2 April, counted as the 101st time from a temple dated 1925. In 2025 the peak window was 11–17 March, with the opening on the evening of 13 March, and more than 90 fishing boats registered. The next solar dates move with the lunar calendar. The rite has been national intangible heritage since 2021.
The port is thị trấn Sông Đốc, huyện Trần Văn Thời, and also xã Sông Đốc. Hòn Đá Bạc is the granite farther along the Gulf, on its own road.

figures.caption: The bridge over the Ông Đốc
figures.alt: A long concrete bridge across the wide Ông Đốc river, with a small boat underneath

gettingThere: Ride west from the city to the port on the Ông Đốc. A local bus links the town and the city station. The ride’s length and the fare are Check on arrival.

legs.heading: From Ca Mau
legs.body: By road west to the port. A local bus also runs between the town and the city station. Road minutes and the fare are Check on arrival.
